quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle in which of these situations?

options.text: At an intersection with a stop sign.
When you see a red light.
When a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, at red lights, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: At a stop sign without a crosswalk, you must stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, stop at the stop line if there is one. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection.

questions.question: A driver taking over-the-counter medicine should:

options.text: Keep driving even if the label warns against it.

questions.explanation: Over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. Check the label for warnings. If you are unsure about driving while taking medicine, ask your doctor or pharmacist.

questions.question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is true?

options.text: Never put an infant in the front seat of a car with airbags.
Airbags can hurt infants and small children, even in minor crashes.
All passengers must wear seat belts or use child restraints.

questions.explanation: Always fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce the risk of injury or death in crashes. Children 12 and under must ride properly restrained in the back seat. Never place a rear-facing infant car seat in the front seat of a vehicle with an airbag.

questions.question: At an intersection with no signs or signals, a vehicle arrives on your right at the same time as you. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to go through first.
Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
Drive through and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk your horn and drive through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Let it pass before you go.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. If possible, move it out of traffic. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Help stop severe bleeding with direct pressure. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Wait for emergency help to arrive.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before it catches up.
Keep driving but stay out of its way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to all emergency vehicles with sirens or flashing red, blue, or white lights. Pull to the right edge of the road when possible. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Hold the wheel straight and slowly lift your foot off the gas.
Keep going at the same speed and steer straight.
Swerve side to side to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the wheel straight and slowly lift your foot off the gas.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel tightly and keep the car straight. Ease off the gas pedal. Do not brake until you have control. Once stable, brake gently and pull to a safe spot off the road.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Just before moving to the other lane, quickly look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: When borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend, you should:

options.text: Not worry because all vehicles are the same.
Not tell your friend you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
Ignore any defects to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Spend a few minutes learning where the controls are and how they work.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spend a few minutes learning where the controls are and how they work.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, spend a few minutes finding the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any defects before driving.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?

options.text: Pull to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull to the side of the road and stop completely.

questions.question: A driver should not pass a car that is stopped at a crosswalk.
questions.explanation: Never pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. Never pass any vehicle at an intersection.

questions.question: If a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Watch what other cars are doing.

questions.explanation: When a police officer is directing traffic, follow the officer's directions instead of the traffic light.

questions.question: You are on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Slow down, move to provide a clear path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to provide a clear path, and stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see or hear an emergency vehicle. Move your car to clear the path and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: You should slow down when driving on:
questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp curves, near pedestrians, and on wet or slippery roads.

questions.question: Drivers who drink alcohol before driving:

options.text: Always know the risks they are taking.
Cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
Are better drivers because they are more careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol impairs judgment, vision, focus, and reaction time. Never drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the road ahead is a divided highway. Stay to the right of the divider.

questions.question: Construction zone signs are orange in color.
questions.explanation: Construction zone signs are orange and diamond-shaped. They are reflective so drivers can see them at night.

questions.question: The best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash is to:

options.text: Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Drive only between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the most effective way to reduce your risk of death or injury while driving.

questions.question: When you see a steady red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.

questions.explanation: A steady red light means stop completely. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red if a sign does not prohibit it.

questions.question: You cannot pass a school bus when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: When you see a school bus with flashing red lights, you must stop before reaching it. Stay stopped until the lights turn off. On a divided road, drivers on the opposite side do not have to stop.

questions.question: Who must wear a properly fastened safety belt in a moving vehicle?
questions.explanation: Everyone in the vehicle must wear a safety belt. Drivers can be cited if they or any passenger under 16 is not wearing one. Passengers 16 and older can also be cited for not wearing a safety belt.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving

questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, your eyes off the road, or your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: You should signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb because:

options.text: It is only necessary when other traffic is near.
It is a good habit and the law requires it.
It is only necessary during the move, not before.
It is not necessary if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a good habit and the law requires it.
questions.explanation: Signal your intentions well before turning or changing lanes. The law requires you to signal at least 100 feet before moving left or right. Always signal before pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: What color are highway signs that show the distance to the next exit?
questions.explanation: Destination signs are green with white letters or symbols.
